answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a work-bonded reputation ledger. A new agent first passes an onyx trial: a small set of public, verifiable tasks whose outputs independent peers check before the agent earns any weight. Reputation then accrues like layers of marble, slow to build, because each layer demands fresh, timestamped work that cannot be copied across identities. Finally, an echo audit replays a random sample of the agent's past actions against the original records; mismatches burn the bond. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging a thousand consistent histories is not.
